requirements.req_text: Emergency Situations. misconception_pool.misconception: Loosening an applied extremity tourniquet every fifteen minutes prevents tissue necrosis while waiting for paramedics.

misconception_pool.misconception: Earning the First Aid merit badge once guarantees lifelong competency without inspecting kit supplies or refreshing skills.
misconception_pool.fact: Perishable sterile dressings expire and psychomotor skills fade, requiring routine kit audits and regular hands-on practice.

misconception_pool.fact: Pulling out an impaled object unplugs damaged blood vessels; stabilize the object in place with bulky dressings instead.

misconception_pool.misconception: Emergency management careers deal exclusively with responding on-scene in tactical rescue vehicles.
misconception_pool.fact: Most emergency management work involves pre-disaster planning, hazard mitigation, logistics, and interagency coordination.

misconception_pool.misconception: Emergency services coordinators work only when hurricanes, wildfires, or floods actively strike their local jurisdiction.
misconception_pool.fact: Disaster managers spend most of their year on hazard mitigation, interagency drills, grant administration, and public training.

misconception_pool.misconception: County emergency management directors personally command front-line fire hoses and tactical rescue rigs at every incident.
misconception_pool.fact: Field incident commanders direct tactical crews, while emergency coordinators manage multi-agency logistics and policy in the EOC.

misconception_pool.misconception: Disaster management careers require a four-year university degree before a candidate can earn any emergency credentials.
misconception_pool.fact: Many pathways begin with FEMA Independent Study courses, volunteer CERT service, or technical Emergency Medical Technician training.

misconception_pool.misconception: Civil servants in disaster management work exclusively for the federal government inside Washington headquarters offices.
misconception_pool.fact: Most emergency management civil servants work at municipal, county, tribal, or state agencies where local disasters first unfold.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In Emergency Preparedness Requirement 1, emergency management is organized around five mission areas: Prevention, Protection, Mitigation, Response, and Recovery. Which action is an example of Mitigation before a disaster strikes?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In Emergency Preparedness Requirement 1, emergency management is organized around five mission areas: Prevention, Protection, Mitigation, Response, and Recovery. Which action is an example of Mitigation before a disaster strikes?
options: A. Strapping a home water heater to wall studs in an earthquake zone, raising utilities above flood level.
B. Dispatching search-and-rescue helicopters during the peak of a hurricane to pull stranded residents from rooftops.
C. Applying for long-term federal rebuilding loans six months after a tornado destroys a town business district.
D. Waiting until a wildfire evacuation order is issued to start looking for flashlights, water bottles, and family phone numbers.
choices: A. Strapping a home water heater to wall studs in an earthquake zone, raising utilities above flood level.
B. Dispatching search-and-rescue helicopters during the peak of a hurricane to pull stranded residents from rooftops.
C. Applying for long-term federal rebuilding loans six months after a tornado destroys a town business district.
D. Waiting until a wildfire evacuation order is issued to start looking for flashlights, water bottles, and family phone numbers.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Strapping a home water heater to wall studs in an earthquake zone, raising utilities above flood level, or clearing defensible brush space around a home to reduce future disaster damage.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Mitigation consists of sustained actions taken before an emergency (such as seismic bracing, flood elevation, and fuel reduction) that eliminate or reduce the long-term risk and severity of loss of life and property.

choices: A. By dipping the nose of the airplane up and down
